Install Neon Bay as an app

Installing puts a Neon Bay icon on your home screen / app list. It opens full-screen like a real game app — no browser bars — and loads fast, even offline. Pick your device:

  1. Android (Chrome / Edge): tap the ⋮ menu at the top right → Install app (or Add to Home screen) → Install. If the one-tap INSTALL GAME button on the start screen offered an install prompt, that does the same thing.
  2. iPhone / iPad (Safari): tap the Share button → Add to Home Screen → Add.
  3. Computer (Chrome / Edge): click the install icon at the right end of the address bar, or open the ⋮ menu → Install Neon Bay / Save and share → Install.

Tip: install from one of the public links (Render or GitHub Pages) rather than a preview, so the icon points at the live game.

Publish Neon Bay on GitHub Pages — free

Your GitHub is HARI30015. This game is already a static website (index.html + assets/three.min.js), so GitHub can host it for free — no server needed. Anyone with the link can play. Keep it separate: use a brand-new neon-bay repo with only Neon Bay files — do not mix it into your other repos.

Your public link will be:
https://HARI30015.github.io/neon-bay/
That link goes live only after you finish the 4 steps below and GitHub Pages finishes its first build (usually 1–2 minutes).
  1. Create the repo: go to github.com/new → name it neon-bay → Public → Create repository.
  2. Add the game files: in the repo, Add file → Upload files → upload index.html and the whole assets folder (it must keep assets/three.min.js inside it). Commit the upload. Tip: tap Download README below and upload that file too.
  3. Turn on Pages: repo Settings → Pages → Source: Deploy from a branch → Branch: main, folder / (root) → Save.
  4. Share the link: wait for the green “Your site is live” message on that same Pages screen, then share your link above.

Want me to do a step for you? Just say the step number in chat and I’ll guide you through that one screen — I’ll ask before using anything from your account.
